title: FreeAgent vs Xero: Which Is Right for UK Contractors in 2026?

html:
If your accountant already includes FreeAgent free in your monthly package, does it even make sense to pay separately for Xero? Most comparison articles skip straight past this question. They treat FreeAgent and Xero as two products you're choosing between in a vacuum, ignoring the most common real-world scenario: you're picking an accountancy firm, and the software comes with it.

Choosing the wrong accounting software costs you time and money every month. We've seen contractors spend hours reconciling data in a platform their accountant can't access properly, then pay again for the tax advice that should have been built into the relationship from day one. This guide cuts through the marketing noise and gives you a clear verdict by business type.

By the end, you'll know exactly how FreeAgent and Xero compare on pricing, Making Tax Digital compliance, and day-to-day usability for UK contractors and freelancers. You'll also understand why the bundled-software question changes the entire calculation - and what that means for limited company directors, sole traders, and landlords specifically.

If you're already looking for an accountant who includes cloud software as standard, take a look at our affordable monthly accounting packages for contractors and freelancers before reading on.

FreeAgent vs Xero: Why the Right Answer Depends on How You Work, Not Just What the Software Does

Every vendor comparison you'll find online frames this as a features race. Xero has 1,000+ third-party app integrations. FreeAgent has a cleaner interface for sole traders. Both handle bank feeds and invoicing. Both are cloud accounting platforms. At the feature level, the gap is smaller than either company's marketing suggests.

The question that actually matters for most UK contractors and freelancers is this: are you self-managing your accounts, or are you working with an accountant? Because that single variable changes which platform makes sense entirely.

Xero is built for businesses that want to run their own bookkeeping, with an accountant dipping in periodically to review. Its ecosystem of third-party apps, its AI-driven automation tools, and its multi-currency transaction handling all assume a business owner who is actively engaged with the software day to day. That's a legitimate use case - but it's not the typical profile of a Bristol-based IT contractor or management consultant who wants to focus on billable work and leave the accounting and finance part to us.

FreeAgent, by contrast, was designed from the ground up for freelancers, contractors, and small limited companies in the UK. Its self assessment tax return filing, corporation tax estimates, and MTD compliance tools are built into the core product rather than bolted on. And critically, it was built to be shared with an accountant - not just accessed by one.

What You Actually Get With FreeAgent in 2026 (Features, Pricing, and MTD Readiness)

FreeAgent's core feature set covers invoicing, expense tracking, bank feeds, payroll, self assessment tax returns, corporation tax filing for micro-companies, and Making Tax Digital submissions. The dashboard gives you real-time visibility of your tax position throughout the year - not just at year-end - which is genuinely useful for contractors managing salary and dividend income.

The FreeAgent Smart Capture feature, included in our Sole Trader MTD with Bookkeeping package, lets you photograph receipts and have them automatically categorised. For a busy engineer or graphic designer who accumulates expenses across multiple projects, this removes a significant admin burden.

On MTD readiness: FreeAgent handles both MTD for VAT and MTD for Income Tax Self Assessment (MTD for ITSA). The GOV.UK guidance on Making Tax Digital for Income Tax confirms that sole traders and landlords with income over £50,000 are now mandated to use MTD-compatible software for quarterly submissions. FreeAgent submits these directly to HMRC, which matters enormously if you're a sole trader or landlord approaching that threshold.

Standalone FreeAgent pricing starts at around £19/month for sole traders and rises for limited companies, though these prices change with promotional periods. The more relevant figure for most of our clients is zero - because Focus Accountancy includes FreeAgent in every package, from £25 a month per property for Rental Accounts upwards.

Does FreeAgent handle Making Tax Digital submissions?

Yes, FreeAgent is fully MTD-compatible for both VAT and Income Tax Self Assessment. It submits quarterly updates directly to HMRC, which means sole traders and landlords caught by the MTD for ITSA mandates don't need separate bridging software. The platform also tracks your cumulative income against the MTD thresholds [CONFIRM: FreeAgent threshold-tracking feature], so you can see when you're approaching a compliance obligation before it becomes urgent. For landlords with multiple properties, this real-time visibility is particularly valuable.

Can my accountant access FreeAgent on my behalf?

Yes, and this is one of FreeAgent's most practical advantages for anyone working with a dedicated accountant. Your accountant gets their own login with full access to your data, meaning they can file your tax returns, review your bookkeeping, and flag issues without you needing to export spreadsheets or send documents back and forth. At Focus Accountancy, we use this access to conduct quarterly FreeAgent reviews for clients on our higher-tier packages, checking categorisation, flagging potential tax savings, and keeping everything ready for year-end. It's a genuinely collaborative setup rather than a software handoff.

What You Actually Get With Xero in 2026 (Features, Pricing, and Where It Pulls Ahead)

Xero is a more powerful platform for businesses with complex needs. Its ecosystem of over 1,000 third-party app integrations covers everything from project management to e-commerce inventory, and its AI-driven automation handles bank reconciliation, expense categorisation, and cash flow forecasting at a level FreeAgent doesn't match. For a growing SME with multiple employees, a sales team, and international clients, Xero's depth is genuinely useful.

The Xero UK pricing plans currently start at £18/month for the Ignite plan, rising to £70/month for the Ultimate plan, which includes payroll for up to 10 people (prices before VAT and any introductory discount). These are standalone software costs - your accountant fees are separate on top.

Xero also handles MTD for VAT and is MTD for ITSA compatible, so compliance isn't a differentiator between the two platforms. Where Xero genuinely pulls ahead is in multi-currency transactions, advanced reporting, and the breadth of its integration ecosystem. If you're running an e-commerce business, managing a team of ten, or dealing with international invoicing regularly, Xero's additional capability is worth the extra cost.

For a typical UK contractor billing one or two clients in sterling, running a single-director limited company, and wanting their accountant to handle the tax side? Most of Xero's advanced features simply go unused.

Is Xero worth the cost for a small limited company?

For a small limited company with straightforward finances, Xero's cost is harder to justify when FreeAgent is available free through an accountancy package. Xero's strength lies in its integrations and scalability, but a single-director contractor company rarely needs 1,000 app connections or advanced multi-currency reporting. If you're already paying a monthly accountancy fee that includes FreeAgent, adding Xero on top means paying twice for cloud accounting software - and potentially creating a disconnect between the tool you're using and the one your accountant works in most efficiently.

Head-to-Head Comparison: FreeAgent vs Xero for UK Contractors, Sole Traders, and Landlords

Here's how the two platforms compare across the features that matter most to the business types Focus Accountancy works with every day.

Feature FreeAgent Xero
Invoicing Clean, simple, with automatic payment reminders More customisable, supports recurring invoices and multi-currency
Bank feeds Direct bank integration with major UK banks Direct bank integration, broader international bank support
Payroll Built-in, handles RTI submissions to HMRC Included from the Grow plan upwards (paid extra on Ignite), more scalable for larger teams
MTD for VAT Yes, direct HMRC submission Yes, direct HMRC submission
MTD for ITSA Yes, quarterly submissions built in Yes, MTD-compatible
Self assessment filing Yes, files directly to HMRC Files MTD for Income Tax quarterly updates and the final declaration
Corporation tax filing Yes, for most micro-entities Yes, with the paid Company Accounts and Tax add-on (simple micro-entities)
Third-party integrations Focused selection of key tools 1,000+ apps via Xero App Store
Mobile access iOS and Android app, well-reviewed iOS and Android app, feature-rich
Ease of use for non-accountants Designed specifically for freelancers and contractors More powerful but steeper learning curve
Accountant collaboration Seamless shared access, built for accountant-client workflow Good accountant access, but less optimised for UK contractor workflow

A practical difference for UK contractors is that FreeAgent's self assessment and corporation tax filing comes as part of the subscription. Xero now files corporation tax returns too, but only through a paid add-on aimed at simple companies. When FreeAgent is your shared platform with your accountant, the entire workflow from bookkeeping to filing happens in one place.

Is FreeAgent better than Xero for contractors?

For most UK contractors operating through a limited company or as a sole trader, FreeAgent is the better fit. It was built specifically for this audience, handles UK tax filings directly, and integrates naturally into an accountant-client relationship. Xero is the stronger choice if you need advanced integrations, multi-currency support, or you're managing a growing team - but for a typical single-director contractor company, those features are rarely needed. The decision becomes even clearer when FreeAgent is included free in your accountancy package.

The Hidden Cost Factor: What Changes When FreeAgent Is Included Free With Your Accountant

This is the calculation most comparison articles ignore. When FreeAgent is bundled into your accountancy package, you're not choosing between two software products. You're choosing between a self-managed Xero setup with a separate accountant, and an all-in package where the software, the filing, and the advice are one monthly fee.

The NatWest angle is worth addressing here too. NatWest and RBS business banking customers can access FreeAgent free as part of their banking relationship. This is a genuine benefit, and it's the full standard version, including MTD for ITSA submissions and free access for your accountant - but it doesn't include the advisory support that comes with a dedicated accountancy package. It's software without the expertise. For a landlord approaching the MTD for ITSA threshold, or a contractor who needs salary and dividend planning, the free banking tier leaves a significant gap.

Is FreeAgent free with NatWest business banking?

Yes, NatWest and RBS business banking customers can access FreeAgent free as part of their account. However, this free tier is the software only. You can submit MTD for ITSA updates yourself and add your accountant as a user for free, but it doesn't include someone to make those submissions on your behalf, tax planning advice, or any of the support that comes with a dedicated accountancy relationship. It's a useful starting point for very early-stage businesses, but it doesn't replace the combination of software plus expert support that comes with a bundled accountancy package.

Making Tax Digital in 2026: Which Platform Keeps You Compliant Without the Headache?

MTD for ITSA is now live for sole traders and landlords with income over £50,000, with the £30,000 threshold following in April 2027. This means quarterly digital submissions to HMRC are no longer optional for a significant portion of the freelancers and landlords we work with at Focus Accountancy.

Both FreeAgent and Xero are MTD-compatible. The practical difference is in how the submissions happen. FreeAgent submits quarterly updates directly from within the platform, and when your accountant has shared access, they can review and submit on your behalf without any additional tools. Xero is also MTD-compatible, but the workflow for a sole trader or landlord typically requires more manual involvement or a bridging step through your accountant's practice software [CONFIRM: Xero now files quarterly updates and the final declaration itself; keep this only if it matches your experience].

For a landlord managing two or three properties, the MTD for ITSA requirement means four quarterly submissions per year plus a final declaration. FreeAgent's rental accounts feature, combined with an accountant who handles the submissions, removes this entirely from the landlord's to-do list. The FreeAgent features page outlines how the platform handles rental income tracking and MTD submissions in detail.

Our Verdict: Which Software Should You Choose Based on Your Business Type?

Here's the honest answer, broken down by the three business types we work with most.

Limited company directors (contractors and consultants): FreeAgent wins. It handles corporation tax estimates, payroll for small teams, invoicing, and bank feeds in a clean interface designed for exactly this use case. When it's included in your accountancy package, the case for paying separately for Xero is very thin unless you have specific integration needs - a CRM connection, advanced project tracking, or multi-currency invoicing for international clients.

Sole traders: FreeAgent wins, particularly for those caught by MTD for ITSA. The direct HMRC filing for self assessment, the quarterly MTD submissions, and the clean mobile access make it the more practical choice. Xero is capable, but its additional complexity doesn't add value for most sole traders billing in sterling to UK clients.

Landlords: FreeAgent wins clearly. The rental accounts feature, MTD for ITSA compliance, and the ability to track income and expenses per property make it purpose-built for this use case. Xero can handle rental income, but it requires more configuration.

Growing SMEs with complex needs: Xero is worth considering. If you're managing a team of five or more, need advanced inventory management, or rely on specific third-party app integrations that FreeAgent doesn't support, Xero's ecosystem justifies the cost. But this profile rarely describes the contractors and freelancers we work with.

Christian, one of our clients, put it well: "Helpful, knowledgeable team that make time to provide jargon-free planning and advice." That's the combination that matters - the right software, used by people who know what they're doing with it, in a relationship where you're not left to figure it out alone.

What is the difference between FreeAgent and Xero?

FreeAgent is built specifically for UK freelancers, contractors, and small limited companies, with direct HMRC filing for self assessment and corporation tax built into the core product. Xero is a broader small business accounting platform with a larger integration ecosystem, more advanced reporting, and better multi-currency support, but it charges extra for corporation tax filing and has a steeper learning curve. For most UK contractors and sole traders, FreeAgent's UK-specific focus and simpler interface make it the more practical daily tool, especially when it's included free in an accountancy package.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which accounting software is best for sole traders in the UK?

For UK sole traders, FreeAgent is generally the stronger choice in 2026, particularly for those affected by MTD for ITSA. It files self assessment tax returns directly to HMRC, handles quarterly MTD submissions without bridging software, and has a clean interface that doesn't require accounting knowledge to use day to day. Xero is capable but adds complexity that most sole traders don't need. If your accountant includes FreeAgent in their package, the decision is straightforward: you get purpose-built software and expert support for one monthly fee.

What is the difference between FreeAgent and Xero?

The core difference is focus and depth. FreeAgent is purpose-built for UK freelancers, contractors, and small limited companies, with direct HMRC filing for self assessment and corporation tax built in from the start. Xero is a broader platform designed for growing SMEs, with over 1,000 third-party integrations, advanced multi-currency support, and more powerful reporting tools. FreeAgent wins on simplicity and UK tax compliance for small businesses; Xero wins on scalability and integration breadth for more complex operations.

Is FreeAgent better than Xero for contractors?

Yes, for the majority of UK contractors. FreeAgent handles the specific tax obligations of contractor life - corporation tax estimates, dividend tracking, self assessment filing, and MTD submissions - within a single platform that your accountant can access directly. Xero charges extra for corporation tax filing, and its advanced features are largely irrelevant for a single-director limited company. The gap widens further when FreeAgent is included free in your accountancy package, making Xero an additional cost with no clear benefit for most contractors.
